new_reasoning.because: Kimi K2.7-Code shipped June 12 with only Moonshot in-house benchmarks and no independent public scores.
new_reasoning.given: Cheap community runs were never the binding constraint - benchmarker attention is, and it has moved to the K3 successor whose full weights land July 27.
new_reasoning.so_that: An independent, reproducible score still has to land on K2.7-Code itself, on a trusted public coding suite, before attention leaves it entirely.
new_reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; an independent SWE-bench Verified or Terminal-Bench result on K2.7-Code, not on its successor.
new_reasoning.plain_language: Outsiders can easily test this open coding model, but their attention has already jumped to its newer sibling.

reason: Applied the 2026-07-19 stale judgement. Bridge validation.e2edb356aab208d7 (2026-07-17) documents Moonshot shipping the K3 successor - a 2.8T open mixture-of-experts model, first on Frontend Code Arena at 1,679, fourth of 189 on the Artificial Analysis index, full weights due July 27 - and says in as many words that this is the successor on an arena, not K2.7-Code on SWE-bench. The old given, that open downloadable weights and an agentic-coding target make community public-suite runs cheap, is still mechanically true but was never the constraint that decides this: an independent maintainer with finite GPU budget now has little reason to run the superseded model through SWE-bench Verified before the Q3 close. The given and so_that now name successor-model displacement as the live threat to landing. The claim and the Q3 2026 window are unchanged.
